references.text: The laws concerning lepers who must live outside the camp, as detailed in Leviticus where the leper is to dwell alone outside the camp
Regulations regarding men with a discharge and their uncleanness, which form the basis for expulsion from the camp
Rules about uncleanness through contact with a dead body, which forbid touching the dead and render a person unclean
Detailed regulations concerning uncleanness from touching dead bodies and the purification process
Miriam was expelled from the camp for seven days because of leprosy, illustrating the practice described in the verse
Soldiers who had killed or touched the dead had to stay outside the camp for seven days for purification
Regulations about uncleanness in the camp and that the unclean person must go out of the camp
Four leprous men who lived outside the city gate, in accordance with the law requiring lepers to be kept outside the camp
